newsitem.title: CANADA: Westcoast work to cut B.C. gas plant output.
newsitem.headline: Westcoast work to cut B.C. gas plant output.

text.p: Westcoast Energy Inc said on Friday that rescheduled work at the company's McMahon natural gas plant in northeast British Columbia would begin on Saturday, reducing capacity for three days.
Westcoast said processing output from the 700 million cubic feet per day plant, the company's biggest, would be reduced to 76 percent on Saturday, 82 percent on Sunday and 97 percent on Monday.
"We have some acidizing of our processing equipment to reduce foaming problems, said Don Berkeley, Westcoast's manager of gas control and measurement.

He said the work had been scheduled to start on January 9, but was pushed back after a fire on Monday in an administration building at the company's Charley Lake office disabled field communication systems.
"Because of the delay, we have two processing trains that we have to do and we're going to do them back to back," Berkeley said.

Spot natural gas prices at Sumas, on the B.C.-Washington border, were quoted in a wide rage of US$3.10-US$3.50 per million British thermal units with an average of about US$3.40 on Friday. That was up from up from US$3.07 per mmBtu on Thursday.
